holidays.name: World Mosquito Day
holidays.description: A day to think about the tiny insect that is arguably the deadliest animal on Earth. It's observed with a mix of science, awareness campaigns, and a lot of swatting. Celebrate by dumping standing water, checking your window screens, and thanking the researchers who work on malaria prevention.
holidays.origin: It marks the discovery made by British doctor Sir Ronald Ross in 1897. He found that female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria to humans. Ross later won a Nobel Prize for the work, and the day has been observed since the early 20th century.
holidays.funFact: Only female mosquitoes bite. They need the protein in blood to develop their eggs, and males feed on nectar.

holidays.name: National Bacon Lover's Day
holidays.description: A day for devoted fans of crispy, smoky, salty bacon. Fry it, wrap it around something, or crumble it onto anything you like. Anything goes today, from maple-glazed strips to bacon-topped desserts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among breakfast fans and food bloggers.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'bringing home the bacon' is often traced to a medieval English tradition at Dunmow. A couple who could swear they hadn't argued for a year and a day won a side of bacon.

holidays.name: National Radio Day
holidays.description: A day to tune in and honor the medium that has soundtracked road trips, kitchens, and late-night confessions for over a century. Crank up a favorite station, call in a song request, or spend some time with an old-school transistor radio.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance that's often linked to the early days of commercial broadcasting. In 1920, Detroit station WWJ began regular commercial radio programming on August 20.
holidays.funFact: WWJ in Detroit is one of the longest-running commercial radio stations in the United States. It is still on the air today.
